summary: The Wildlife Road Crossings Program Reauthorization Act of 2025 amends the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to reauthorize and fund the wildlife crossings program through fiscal years 2026 through 2031, removing the word "pilot" from its title and updating program administration, federal cost shares for Indian Tribes, and technical assistance rules.

affected_groups.effect: Receive a 100 percent Federal cost share for project grants and gain access to technical and application assistance funded by the program.
Authorized to retain a portion of funds for grant administration and provide technical assistance through government, private, or nonprofit entities.

key_provisions: Authorizes $200,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2031 for the wildlife crossings program.
Changes the program name and references by removing the term "pilot" throughout the relevant sections of law.
Sets the Federal cost share for project grants submitted by Indian Tribes to 100 percent.
Allows the Secretary to use up to half of 1 percent of authorized funds to provide application and technical assistance to Indian Tribes.
Allows the Secretary to retain up to half of 1 percent of available funds for grant administration, review, and related requirements.
Provides that any unobligated funds for a fiscal year remain available until expended in addition to amounts otherwise available.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact criteria for winning grant awards.
Specific details on how the broader public outside of tribal entities will interact with the program.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Wildlife Road Crossings Program Reauthorization Act of 2025 amends the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to reauthorize and fund the wildlife crossings program through fiscal years 2026 through 2031, removing the word "pilot" from its title and updating program administration, federal cost shares for Indian Tribes, and technical assistance rules.
summary_detail.significance: The bill continues and funds a federal transportation-related program aimed at wildlife road crossings, allocating $200 million annually from fiscal year 2026 through 2031 and establishing dedicated administrative and tribal support provisions.
